input: wall is a list of r rows, 0 <= r <= 4294967295. Each nonempty row is a list of positive integer brick widths, with row length <= 4294967295. For r > 0 all row sums must equal the same positive safe integer W <= 9007199254740991. Empty wall is accepted. Rows may share identities because they are read only. Integers are plain int, excluding bool; lists and strings are ordinary list/str values, not subclasses. No concurrent mutation, getters or modified standard built-ins are allowed. Preconditions are not checked at runtime. Declared size bounds are not a guarantee of available memory or completion within an unqualified runtime budget.
return: The minimum number of bricks crossed by one vertical line strictly inside the common wall width. A line on an internal brick boundary does not cross that brick; outer edges at zero and W are forbidden. Empty wall returns 0. If no internal boundary exists, every row is crossed.
mutation_aliasing: Inputs, ordering and caller-owned containers remain unchanged. The Solution instance retains no state; separate calls share no mutable result state. A private map counts internal prefix positions. No row or brick width is modified, including when input rows alias.
numeric: Positive widths ensure every recorded prefix lies strictly between zero and W, with exact safe additions. Edge frequencies and aligned are at most r; r - aligned is a nonnegative safe integer. The final brick of each row is excluded, so the forbidden outer boundary is never counted.
complexity: O(B + 1) prefix/map operations for B total bricks and O(E + 1) retained map entries for E distinct internal edge positions. No row slices are allocated.
